The meaning is that they are not trees that bear fruit and grow, but rather timber propped against a wall.

Then He censured them for cowardice, saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They think every cry is against them﴾, that is, they do not hear any sound without thinking that they have been reached, because of the terror in their hearts, that God will expose their secrets. This is an exaggeration of their cowardice. They recited, on this meaning:

*Even if it were a sparrow, you would think it*
*A marked horse calling out to ʿUbayd and Azram.*

That is: even if a sparrow were to fly, you would think, from your cowardice, that it was horsemen calling out to those two tribes.

God, Exalted is He, says: ﴿They are the enemy, so beware of them﴾, that is, do not trust them with your secret, for they are spies for your enemies among the unbelievers. ﴿God fight them! How they are turned away!﴾ It is explained in [Surah al-Tawba: 30].

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on Surah 63, verses 5–8:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come, the Messenger of God will ask forgiveness for you," they turn their heads aside﴾. We have already explained its occasion of revelation at the beginning of the surah. ﴿They turn their heads aside﴾. Nafi', al-Mufaddal (on the authority of Asim), and Ya'qub recited "lawwaw" with the light (single-consonant) form. Abu 'Ubayda preferred the doubled form and said: "Because they did this again and again." Mujahid said: "When it was said to Abdullah ibn Ubayy, 'Come, the Messenger of God will ask forgiveness for you,' he turned his head aside, and said, 'What did I say?'" Muqatil said: "They inclined their heads out of aversion to seeking forgiveness." Al-Farra' said: "They shook them in mockery of the Prophet and his supplication."

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And you see them turning away﴾, meaning: they turn away from seeking forgiveness. ﴿While they are arrogant﴾, meaning: they are too proud for that. Then He mentioned that his asking forgiveness for them would not benefit them, in His words: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾. Abu Ja'far recited "a-astaghfarta" with the extended alif.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God, until they disperse"﴾. We have already explained that this is the statement of Ibn Ubayy. ﴿Yanfaddu'' (until they disperse)﴾ means: until they scatter. ﴿And to God belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth﴾. The exegetes said: the treasuries of the heavens are rain, and the treasuries of the earth are vegetation. The meaning is: He is the Provider of these emigrants, not of those. ﴿But the hypocrites do not understand﴾, meaning: they do not know that God is the one who provides for them while these people spend on them. ﴿They say, "If we return to Medina"﴾ from this campaign, which has already been mentioned, and this is the statement of Ibn Ubayy. ﴿The more honored will surely expel the more humble﴾. He meant himself by "the more honored," and by "the more humble" he meant the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Al-Hasan recited "lanukhrijanna" with a dammah on the nun and a kasrah on the ra', and "al-a'azza" with a fathah on the zay. "Al-adhall" is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal), based on the permissibility of making the circumstantial state definite, or on the addition of "al" to it, or on the assumption of an implied "mithl" (like). The meaning is: "We will expel him in a state of humiliation, whatever form humiliation takes." All of them put "al-adhall" in the accusative. God, Mighty and Majestic, then replied to this, saying: ﴿But honor belongs to God, and to His Messenger, and to the believers﴾. Honor here means protection and strength, ﴿through God's granting them might and His support﴾. ﴿But the hypocrites do not know﴾ this.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 63, verse 9–11:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Let not your wealth and your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah﴾, meaning: let them not preoccupy you. Regarding the intended meaning of "the remembrance of Allah" here, there are four opinions.

The first: obedience to Allah in jihad. This was said by Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: the obligatory prayer (al-salat al-maktubah). This was said by 'Ata' and Muqatil.

The third: the obligatory duties, including the prayer and others. This was said by al-Dahhak.

The fourth: that it is on its general sense. Al-Zajjaj said: "He urged them by this to persist in remembrance."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And spend from what We have provided you﴾. Regarding this spending there are three opinions.

The first: that it is the zakat on wealth. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: that it is spending on the obligatory rights attached to wealth, such as zakat, hajj, and the like. This meaning is related from al-Dahhak. (p-278) The third: that it is voluntary charity (sadaqat al-tatawwu'), mentioned by al-Mawardi. According to this, the command is one of recommendation (nadb), whereas according to the preceding views it is a command of obligation (wujub).

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Before death comes to one of you﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: that is, before he witnesses what makes him know that he is dying.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿My Lord, if only You would delay me﴾, meaning: "Why not delay me" ﴿for a short term﴾. He means by this the seeking of an extension of his term, so that he may give charity and purify (his wealth), and this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿so I would give charity﴾. Abu 'Ubayda said: ﴿fa-assaddaqa﴾ is in the accusative (naṣb), because every response introduced by "fa" following an interrogative is in the accusative. You say: "Who is with you, so that I may come to you (fa-ataya)?" "Why did you not do such-and-such, so that I may do such-and-such (fa-af'ala)?" Then follows ﴿and I would be among the righteous﴾ without a waw. Abu 'Amr said: it is actually "wa-akun" (and I would be), and the waw was dropped from the written text, just as "Abu Jad, Abjad" is written without its letters being spelled out. Thus Abu 'Amr reads it "wa-akūna" with the waw and the nun in the accusative. The rest read "wa-akun" without the waw. Al-Zajjaj said: whoever reads "wa-akūna" follows the wording of "fa-assaddaqa." Whoever reads "akun" in the jussive follows the position of "fa-assaddaqa," because the meaning is: "If You delay me, I shall give charity and I shall be among the righteous."

Abu Salih related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿fa-assaddaqa﴾, that is, "I shall purify my wealth," ﴿and I would be among the righteous﴾, that is, "I shall perform hajj with the believers." He said regarding His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾, that the meaning is: of what you do of denial regarding charity. Muqatil said: he means the hypocrites. al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas: No one dies who had wealth on which he did not pay zakat and who was able to perform hajj but did not perform it, except that he asks Allah for a return at the time of death. They said to him: "Only the disbelievers ask for a return." He said: "I recite to you a Qur'an concerning it," and then he recited this verse.
